query: What does emotionally unavailable actually mean?

per_question.q: Which page leaves the reader more in charge of changing this?
per_question.why: In page A, keeping the seminar link outside of the 'identify-box' avoids turning the reader's self-recognition into an immediate external program pitch.

per_question.q: Which page asks less of the reader before it has earned it?
per_question.why: Page B embeds an external promotional link directly inside the introductory identification callout box before the reader has even read the opening paragraphs, whereas Page A lets the identification box conclude on its own terms.

per_question.q: Which page treats the reader as the person who does the work, rather than as someone who has to be sent somewhere?
per_question.why: By leaving the identify box clean of promotional seminar links, Page A lets the reflection rest with the reader rather than bundling self-reflection into a signpost to a workshop.

per_question.q: Which page gives the reader more room to decide for themselves what to do next?
per_question.why: Separating the external link from the callout container allows the diagnostic sentences to stand on their own without immediately directing action.

per_question.q: Which page puts the author's own history to better use for the reader?
per_question.why: The author's history appears later under 'How Can I Tell If I Am the Emotionally Unavailable One?', but Page A sets up a cleaner, less commercially urgent context for personal disclosure.

per_question.q: Which page makes the first screen feel more like the reader's own words?
per_question.why: Placing the seminar link at the bottom of the container leaves the plain text directly following the box slightly less cluttered with standalone links.

per_question.q: Which page's opening is easier to read straight through without being interrupted?
per_question.why: In Page B, the standalone markdown paragraph starting with 'There is a small move...' follows cleanly after the callout box without an intervening isolated link line.

per_question.q: Which page makes a reader likelier to think "that is me" in the first thirty seconds?
per_question.why: The identify-box in Page A concludes cleanly with the resonant thought 'the cost is a life where the people closest to you never quite find out who is in there', allowing the realization to land without immediately pivoting to a seminar link.

per_question.q: Which page keeps its argument moving without a detour that breaks the thread?
per_question.why: The identify callout box remains purely about the reader's internal rules, preventing an in-box commercial diversion.

per_question.q: Which page makes it easier to follow the line from the question at the top to the answer?
per_question.why: Keeping the identify box focused strictly on definition and internal lines maintains a cleaner conceptual progression from short answer to internal experience.

A: The link placed directly below the identify-box sits as an isolated one-line paragraph before the prose narrative begins.
B: Tucking the seminar link into the identify-box interrupts the reader's inward recognition with promotional callout text.

first_screen: Page A leaves the reader more in charge because the identify box ends on an empowering and resonant diagnostic statement rather than culminating in a seminar pitch.
provenance: Both pages provide identical attributions and citations, including Biringen's Emotional Availability Scales and Developmental Review 2014.
